prompt:
Create a NEW corrected FRONT-FACING COLLAPSE of the attached ORIGINAL ASHVEIL ash crow. Keep this same charcoal corvid identity, crisp detailed pixel art, two wings, two feet, pointed black beak, dark eyes and ash-blue feather highlights. Use the existing FRONT row's correct initial front view as anatomy reference, but repair its last two poses: they incorrectly rotated the entire bird to face LEFT. They must remain facing FRONT toward the bottom of the image when collapsing.

EXACTLY TWO ROWS by TWO COLUMNS, four whole birds on true transparent RGBA, all four from the SAME elevated FRONT camera. Reading order top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right. This is not four directions, no side or back views anywhere. Huge empty transparent gutters, bird occupies only central half of each cell; no floor/shadow/grid/labels/text/props/effects/blood, no clipping or overlap.

1 top-left: front-facing bird buckles, knees flex, beak foreshortened toward bottom, head lowers. 2 top-right: front-facing bird stumbles low and one wing braces on ground, other wing attached, chest and beak STILL toward bottom. 3 bottom-left: bird collapses FORWARD ONTO ITS BREAST while facing viewer, both folded wing shoulders visible symmetrically left and right, head/beak low at LOWER CENTER toward viewer, legs tuck behind under body and tail remains behind the head toward TOP; never turn beak to left/right edge. 4 bottom-right: inert breast-down front-facing crow, closed eyes, foreshortened beak at LOWER CENTER near ground, two folded wings symmetrically flanking back, tail behind toward top and feet tucked underneath. It may slump slightly but the entire long head-tail axis stays TOP-to-BOTTOM rather than left-to-right. Do not use the side-facing dead-bird pose. Four distinct consecutive original collapse poses, same body/head size and same frontal elevated game camera.
